content: This whole procedure is a LOT easier if you just completely remove the left and right front tensioner thingies. Just put them off to the side, this will give you all the belt length in the world you might need. Just skip step 36

One of the most important steps is here and the next steps that you need to adjust the upper and lower belt lengths to be exactly the same length. For the left belts and right belts of course. That’s also stated in step 21 „ When installing the belts into the carriage, verify that all four belt ends have the exact same number of protruding teeth from the carriage.“. Also ensure to carry out the belt tensioning later very carefully (see https://help.prusa3d.com/article/adjusting-belt-tension-core-one-core-one-indx-core-one-l_845048). 

If there is only the difference of one belt tooth you might end up with serious misaligned layers / severe quality and need to disassemble the extender, x- and y-motors again!

Everyone struggling with fixing the belts to the nextruder holder, follow this tip:

Insert a zip tie through the linear rail mount screw holes (2 left; in the first picture: one below the thumb). Once you have aligned the length to be flush with the holder, you can pull the zip tie close and basically forget about it until you mount the thing to the linear rail. And since its mounted in the screw holes, you won't forget about the zip accidentally.

replies.content: If there were a Nobel Prize for instruction manual comments, this one would win hands down. The most difficult part of the whole printer assembly is getting the belt alignment right on the holder. The zip tie makes it much much easier. DO THIS.
I second the motion.  This one tip saved me an ungodly amount of frustration.  Prusa, please make this part of the instructions.
Just out of curiosity if you fit the correct length. Why not just loosen the tensioners totally and do these last?

content: The original belts would use a measurement such as “4 to 5 teeth” to leave hanging. Gen 2 upgrade changes this to be flush with the metal and I think this is a better way to make sure the belt lengths are pulled to the right length. My orignal belt kept slipping teeth, but I guess 3 to 2 teeth tolerance was enough for the old belt
